Answers from the filed court record

Each page below answers one question using verbatim passages from the filed Michigan court documents, citing the filing by name and page. The answers are quotations, not summaries: nothing on these pages paraphrases or interprets a filing, and nothing is generated.

  • When is the next motion hearing in Wayne County divorce case 26-104594-DO?

    The hearing date, time, and judge are stated in the Consolidated Notice of Hearing filed July 2, 2026.

  • What Michigan court rule governs appointing a guardian ad litem in a civil case?

    The motion cites the rule and states the standard it applies.

  • Does appointing a guardian ad litem decide anything about the merits of the case?

    The motion states expressly what an appointment does and does not determine.

  • What does the motion to appoint a guardian ad litem ask the court to do?

    The relief requested is set out in the motion filed July 2, 2026 under MCR 2.201(E).

  • What motions are scheduled for hearing on August 26, 2026 in case 26-104594-DO?

    The Consolidated Notice of Hearing lists ten motions set for the same date.

  • Did the plaintiff file an answer to the counterclaim for divorce in case 26-104594-DO?

    An Answer to Part III, Counterclaim for Divorce was filed on the plaintiff's behalf by counsel; the filing is in the record as a scanned document.

What this archive can and cannot answer

The text behind these answers comes from 173 filed PDFs totalling959 pages. 851 pages carry a real text layer and can be quoted directly. A further 77 pages are scanned images that have been put through optical character recognition, which makes them searchable and describable. 31 pages have no usable text at all.

Machine-transcribed pages are never quoted on this site. OCR of these documents interleaves vertical margin text into body lines, so a passage lifted from it can be wrong in ways that read perfectly plausibly. Quoting it would put words in a court document that the document does not contain. Answers that rest on a scanned filing therefore name the filing and the page and link the PDF, without reproducing its words. The build enforces this: a quoted citation to a transcribed page fails and the page does not publish.

This matters for a second reason. If a question is answered only on a page with no usable text, an engine reading text alone would report that the filings do not address it. That would be false. The filings below are affected, and any question touching them should be checked against the PDF directly.

Every filed document in this archive is now searchable. Before transcription, seven filings carried no searchable text at all, including the opposing party’s Answer to Counterclaim, its Motion to Set Aside Default, and the responses to Requests for Admissions.

Filings only partly searchable

15 filings still have pages with no usable text, generally handwritten or photographic exhibits where transcription confidence fell below the threshold and the result was discarded rather than published.
